stem:
An alternating voltage *V* varies with time *t* according to

*V* = 18 cos 40π*t*

where *V* is in V and *t* is in s.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: show that the period is 0.050 s

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.1, sketch the variation of *V* with *t* for values of *t* from *t* = 0 to *t* = 100 ms.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The alternating voltage is rectified to produce an output voltage across a load resistor *R*, as shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]

Fig. 7.3 shows the variation with *t* of the power *P* in the load resistor.

[[fig:f3]]

State three conclusions that can be drawn from Fig. 7.3. The conclusions may be qualitative or quantitative. Use the space for any working.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A blank gridded graph with voltage V / V on the vertical axis and time t / ms from 0 to 100 on the horizontal axis.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A rectification circuit block connected to an alternating voltage input and a load resistor R, with the output voltage indicated across the resistor.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.3
figures.alt: A graph of power P in the load resistor against time t, showing four repeating peaks between 0 and 100 ms.
